# Company 037 — Internal Policy Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:037`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:037`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-037-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no policy publication, employee attestation, legal acceptance or disciplinary action.

## Business identity

Purpose: maintain internal company policies as versioned, source-backed operational controls tied to regulations, business processes, employee acknowledgments, training and exception workflows.

Problem: policies go stale, conflict with one another, fail to map to actual systems/workflows and become disconnected from new regulations or business changes.

Value: one governed policy lifecycle from draft through review, communication, acknowledgment, exception and evidence.

## Product tree

Policy Library; Drafting/Template Studio; Policy Versioning/Supersession; Conflict/Overlap Detection; Regulation/Control Mapping; Procedure/Workflow Mapping; Owner/Reviewer Registry; Review Calendar; Employee/Role Applicability; Acknowledgment Tracking; Training Linkage; Exception/Waiver Management; Policy Q&A with Citations; Change Summaries; Employee Portal; Audit/Evidence Export; Policy Analytics; API/OEM; Vertical/Framework Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: policy ID/title/type, effective/retire dates, scope/roles/locations, source/regulatory refs, owner/reviewer, version/diff, approval state, required acknowledgment, training dependency, exception reason/expiry, conflict status, linked procedures/controls/systems, review frequency, citations, audit, localization/accessibility.

Customers: HR, legal ops, compliance, security, privacy, IT, operations, SMB through enterprise, nonprofits, public contractors, SaaS platforms embedding policy workflows.

Verticals: information security, privacy, HR/workplace, finance controls, acceptable use, AI use, procurement/vendor, incident response, data retention, healthcare admin, public contracting. Legal/regulatory interpretation remains specialist-owned.

## Brain / architecture

Brain compares policy versions, detects contradictions, maps requirements to procedures and drafts revisions/change summaries with citations. It cannot make law, bind employees, publish policy or approve exceptions without authority.

Architecture: policy/version registry, source/control graph, search/RAG, document diff, rules for applicability/reviews, workflow/approval, acknowledgment/training links, exceptions, LLM drafting grounded in approved sources.

## Agent tree

Policy Draft Agent, Conflict Agent, Regulation Mapping Agent, Procedure Mapping Agent, Review Calendar Agent, Acknowledgment Agent, Training Link Agent, Exception/Waiver Agent, Policy Q&A Agent, Change Communication Draft Agent, Evidence/Audit Agent, Localization Agent.

## Deterministic services

Policy registry/versioning; diff; source/control graph; review scheduler; applicability engine; approval workflow; acknowledgment ledger; training status; exception expiry; notification; audit/export; protected publish gate.

## Workflow

Trigger (new rule/periodic review/business change) → identify affected policies → source/impact map → draft diff → conflict/control review → owner/legal/security approval → protected publish → acknowledgment/training → exception handling → evidence → next review.

## Integrations / API / data

HRIS, LMS, identity/roles, GRC/compliance, knowledge bases, ticketing/workflows, regulation monitor, e-sign/acknowledgment, document storage. APIs for policies/versions/applicability/acknowledgments/exceptions/reviews.

Data moat: policy-control-procedure graph, reviewed change corpus, vertical templates and exception patterns; customer policies isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Users/employees/policies/framework packs, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed policy operations, premium change monitoring. Distribution through HR/GRC/security/privacy/knowledge ecosystems and consultants.

## Security/privacy/legal

Policies can reveal security and legal posture. Strict access/role scope, privileged policy handling, no unsupported legal advice, protected publication/attestation, immutable history, retention/legal holds.

## Failure / edge cases

Conflicting approved policies, retroactive effective date, role/location mismatch, unreviewed legal wording, exception outliving policy, training linked to superseded version, employee on leave, translation drift. Use exact versions/effective dates and explicit applicability.

## Scale/overlap

Small handbook → enterprise policy governance platform. Overlap #12 compliance, #16 regulation, #28 knowledge base, #75 access review. #037 owns internal policy lifecycle.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** decision/rule/version/scope/effective-date/supersession records, citations, approval/publish boundaries.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already has rule/decision ledgers; reverse-map policy-pack/applicability contracts.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** company tenant policy namespaces, acknowledgment/training/exception abstractions.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer policy product/templates/integrations.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global regulatory/policy pack ecosystem.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: library/drafting/version/conflict/regulation/procedure/owners/reviews/applicability/ack/training/exceptions/Q&A/change summaries/portal/audit/analytics/API/packs.
2. Feature Tree: identity/scope/dates/sources/owners/diffs/approval/ack/training/exceptions/links/reviews/citations/audit/localization.
3. Customer Tree: HR/legal/compliance/security/privacy/IT/ops/SMB-enterprise/nonprofit/public/SaaS platforms.
4. Vertical Tree: security/privacy/HR/finance/acceptable use/AI/procurement/incidents/retention/health admin/public contracting.
5. Brain Tree: cited compare/conflict/map/draft; legal approval/publishing prohibited.
6. Agent Tree: draft/conflict/regulation/procedure/review/ack/training/exception/Q&A/comms/evidence/localization.
7. Service Tree: registry/version/diff/graph/scheduler/applicability/approval/ack/training/exceptions/notify/audit/publish gate.
8. Workflow Tree: trigger→impact→draft→review→approve→publish→ack/train→exception→evidence→review.
9. Integration Tree: HRIS/LMS/IAM/GRC/knowledge/tickets/regulation/e-sign/docs.
10. Data Tree: policies/versions/sources/controls/procedures/applicability/approvals/acks/exceptions/training.
11. API Tree: policy/version/applicability/ack/exception/review.
12. Monetization Tree: users/employees/policies/packs/enterprise/private/API/OEM/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: HR/GRC/security/privacy/knowledge/consultant ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: monitoring/diffs/conflict/review reminders/drafts; publication/attestation gated.
15. Moat Tree: policy-control-procedure graph, reviewed changes, vertical templates.
16. Platform Tree: policy library→continuous policy governance→enterprise control framework.
17. Risk Tree: legal error, security disclosure, stale/conflicting policy, bad applicability, false acknowledgment.
18. Scale Tree: handbook→multi-department→global enterprise policy plane.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #12/#16/#28/#75 already cover compliance/regulation/knowledge/access.
20. Command Center Dependencies: rule/decision ledgers, policy packs, docs/provenance, scheduler, identity, audit.
21. Design-Now Requirements: versioned scoped effective-date rule/policy contract.
22. Build-Now Requirements: strengthen Command Center policy-pack and applicability seams after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer policy product/templates/employee portal/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: review monitoring/conflict detection/draft preparation/ack tracking run automatically; authorized people approve material policies/exceptions.

## Saturation result

Further branches are compliance/knowledge/training/access modules already represented or policy-pack variants.

# Company 038 — Grant Management Software

**Company ID:** `company:future:038`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:038`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-038-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no live grant hunting, application submission, certification, signature or spending.

## Business identity

Purpose: manage known/authorized grant programs from requirements and application preparation through milestones, budgets, evidence, reporting and closeout.

Problem: grant work involves complex eligibility, documents, deadlines, budget restrictions, deliverables and recurring reports; teams lose evidence or miss obligations.

Value: one structured grant lifecycle with cited requirements, task ownership, budget tracking and audit-ready evidence.

## Product tree

Grant/Program Registry; Requirement/Eligibility Matrix; Application Workspace; Deadline/Milestone Calendar; Document/Evidence Vault; Narrative Drafting Assistant; Budget Builder/Tracker; Collaboration/Assignments; Submission Readiness; Award/Contract Intake; Deliverable/Milestone Tracking; Expense/Budget Compliance; Evidence Collection; Progress/Outcome Reporting; Amendment/Change Request Tracker; Renewal/Continuation Planner; Closeout Checklist; Portfolio Dashboard; Funder/Program Portal (where appropriate); API/OEM; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: program/version/source, applicant entity, eligibility criteria, required forms/docs, deadline/timezone, questions/limits, budget categories, match requirements, restricted/unrestricted funds, deliverables, milestones, reporting cadence, evidence, approvals, amendment history, payment/reimbursement status refs, audit/export.

Customers: nonprofits, education, research/admin teams, local/public entities, community organizations, businesses managing awarded grants, foundations/funders for internal administration, consultants.

Verticals: nonprofit/community, education, research, workforce development, infrastructure, environmental, arts/culture, small-business programs, public health administration. Each program has legal/financial requirements requiring source and specialist review.

## Brain / architecture

Brain interprets program documents, maps requirements, drafts source-backed narratives and tracks gaps. It cannot hunt live grants under current rule, certify eligibility, sign or submit. Deterministic budgets/deadlines/compliance checks own arithmetic/readiness.

Architecture: program/document registry, requirement ontology, project workspace, scheduler, budget ledger, evidence/artifact store, search/RAG with citations, workflow/approval, reporting templates, LLM drafting with source-bound facts.

## Agent tree

Program Intake Agent, Requirement/Eligibility Agent, Application Planner, Narrative Draft Agent, Budget Agent, Document/Evidence Agent, Deadline Agent, Compliance Agent, Milestone Agent, Reporting Agent, Amendment Agent, Closeout Agent, QA/Fact Checker, Collaboration Coordinator.

## Deterministic services

Program/version registry; date scheduler; requirement matrix; document hash/store; budget calculator/ledger; approval workflow; task dependencies; evidence linking; report template engine; audit/export; protected signature/submit/spend gates.

## Workflow

Import authorized grant program → verify source/version → requirements/eligibility matrix → go/no-go owner decision → application plan/assignments → draft/evidence/budget → readiness QA → protected signature/submission → if awarded, create obligation/budget/milestone plan → evidence/expense tracking → report → amendment/renewal → closeout/archive.

## Integrations / API / data

Document storage, accounting, task/project tools, calendars, e-sign, grant portals where authorized, CRM/donor systems, data collection/reporting tools. APIs for programs/requirements/milestones/budgets/evidence/readiness/reports.

Data moat: program requirement ontology, reviewed application/report mappings, budget/closeout workflows and vertical templates. No cross-applicant confidential data sharing.

## Monetization / distribution

Organizations/programs/users, applications/awards, vertical packs, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed administration/migration. Distribution via nonprofit/education/research ecosystems, consultants/accounting partners and grants-management associations. No opportunity hunting now.

## Security/legal/privacy

Applications can include tax/financial/personnel/beneficiary data. Strict isolation, citation, no fabricated outcomes, protected attestations/submissions, audit, retention, financial controls, role separation.

## Failure / edge cases

Program amendment, deadline extension, portal outage, eligibility ambiguity, restricted-cost misclassification, duplicate evidence, reimbursement vs advance confusion, indirect-cost rules, match source change, reporting metric drift, closeout deadline. Preserve program version and explicit uncertainty.

## Scale/overlap

Single organization → multi-program portfolio → enterprise/funder grant operations. Overlap #31 forms, #36 RFPs, #23 obligations, #97 tax only tangential. #038 owns grant lifecycle after a known program is in scope.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** project/workspace, document provenance, temporal obligations, budget/financial controls, protected submission/signature.  
**BUILD NOW:** shared workspace/artifact/scheduler/finance-policy seams after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** company financial isolation, reporting/evidence and portal connector interfaces.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** grant program data/product/templates/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large funder/applicant network and program marketplace.

# Company 039 — Digital Asset Licensing Marketplace

**Company ID:** `company:future:039`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:039`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-039-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no marketplace launch, seller onboarding, payment, royalty, public listing or legal commitment.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide a trustworthy marketplace/infrastructure for licensing reusable digital assets with clear provenance, rights, permitted uses, royalties and buyer/seller tooling.

Problem: digital assets are copied, relicensed and remixed without consistent provenance or machine-readable rights; buyers struggle to verify ownership and permitted use.

Value: rights-aware discovery, transaction evidence, licensing metadata and creator/enterprise workflows.

## Product tree

Asset Marketplace; Asset Registry; Seller Studio; Buyer Workspace; License Template/Policy Engine; Provenance/Authenticity Verification; Rights/Ownership Evidence; Royalty/Revenue Split Ledger; Search/Discovery; Bundles/Collections; Subscription Libraries; Enterprise Team Licensing; White-label/OEM Marketplace; API/SDK; Asset Delivery/CDN; Version/Update Rights; Takedown/Dispute Workflow; Fraud/Copy Detection; Usage/Entitlement Verification; Marketplace Analytics; Partner/Affiliate Layer; Private Enterprise Asset Exchange.

Asset classes: graphics/templates, code/components, prompts/workflows, agent packs, datasets, video/audio, 3D/models, educational assets, document templates, localization packs, evaluation packs. Each class needs specific rights/safety checks.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: seller identity, asset ID/version/hash, source/provenance, ownership evidence, license type, permitted/prohibited uses, commercial/seat/project/territory/duration limits, attribution, derivative rights, AI-training/use flags, exclusivity, pricing, royalties, tax/payment metadata refs, download/entitlement, update history, reporting, dispute/takedown, ratings/reviews, accessibility.

Customers: creators, developers, agencies, businesses, educators, designers, AI/agent builders, enterprises, marketplaces/platforms, OEM/resellers.

Verticals: design, software, AI prompts/agents/evals, data, media/audio/video, education, business templates, localization, gaming/3D. Legal/licensing model differs substantially by asset class.

## Brain / architecture

Brain helps classify assets, detect metadata gaps/possible duplicates, recommend licensing/packaging language and assist discovery. It cannot determine legal ownership conclusively, grant rights the seller lacks, adjudicate disputes or alter payment/royalty terms without authority.

Architecture: asset/provenance registry, object storage/CDN, search/vector/metadata index, entitlement/license policy engine, seller/buyer orgs, billing/payment abstraction, royalty ledger, fraud/hash/similarity service, moderation, audit, dispute workflow, LLM for metadata/search assistance with deterministic rights enforcement.

## Agent tree

Asset Intake Agent, Metadata Agent, Provenance Agent, License Configuration Agent, Similarity/Fraud Agent, Content/Safety Review Agent, Search/Discovery Agent, Bundle/Packaging Agent, Seller Support Agent, Buyer Support Agent, Dispute Intake Agent, Royalty/Reconciliation Agent, Enterprise Licensing Agent, Analytics Agent.

## Deterministic services

Asset registry; hashing/signatures; object delivery; identity/orgs; license/entitlement rules; billing/transaction events; royalty ledger; search/index; download token; usage/quota; moderation queues; dispute/takedown; tax/payment refs; audit/export.

## Workflow

Seller registers → identity/evidence → upload/hash/version → metadata/classification → rights/license configuration → safety/fraud checks → protected publish → buyer discovers → license/price entitlement → protected transaction → delivery token → usage/entitlement evidence → royalty/reconciliation → updates/disputes/takedowns.

## Integrations / API / data

Payment/billing, storage/CDN, developer Git/package ecosystems, design tools, learning platforms, media tooling, provenance/authenticity, tax systems, support/identity. APIs for assets/search/license/entitlement/download/version/provenance/royalty/status.

Data moat: trusted asset/provenance graph, machine-readable license ontology, transaction/entitlement history, similarity fingerprints and curated creator ecosystem. Private enterprise exchanges remain isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Marketplace commission, seller subscription, buyer library subscription, enterprise seats, asset storage/delivery, premium verification, OEM/white-label, API, promoted placement only if transparent, partner/affiliate commission. No payments activated by roadmap.

## Security/privacy/legal

Copyright/IP ownership, trademarks, privacy/likeness, dataset rights, open-source license conflicts, stolen assets, malware in code/files, explicit content/moderation, tax/payment compliance. Strong takedown/dispute evidence, seller identity, no claim to legal adjudication.

## Failure / edge cases

Stolen asset, multiple claimants, open-source code relicensed improperly, derivative work ambiguity, malicious package, version revoked, buyer downloads after refund, territory conflict, AI-generated ownership uncertainty, chargeback, creator account takeover. Use immutable provenance, entitlement checks, quarantine, takedown and dispute holds.

## Scale/platform/overlap

Niche asset marketplace → multi-asset licensing infrastructure → API/OEM/private enterprise exchanges. Overlap #79 provenance, #81 open-source licensing, #69 billing/#70 entitlements. #039 owns commercial asset exchange/licensing.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** asset/provenance/license/entitlement/version identities, rights metadata, protected publish/financial actions, company/customer isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center artifact/provenance/entitlement interfaces after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** billing/entitlement/asset delivery/moderation/dispute abstractions.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** marketplace/customer/seller product/licensing packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large creator network/CDN/global tax/rights operations.

4. Vertical Tree: design/code/AI/data/media/education/templates/localization/gaming-3D.
5. Brain Tree: metadata/discovery/similarity/licensing assistance; ownership/legal decisions gated.
6. Agent Tree: intake/metadata/provenance/license/fraud/safety/search/packaging/support/dispute/royalty/enterprise/analytics.
7. Service Tree: asset/hash/storage/identity/license/entitlement/billing/royalty/search/download/moderation/dispute/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: register→verify→upload→rights→checks→publish→license→transact→deliver→reconcile→update/dispute.
9. Integration Tree: payment/storage/Git/design/learning/media/provenance/tax/support/IAM.
10. Data Tree: assets/versions/provenance/licenses/owners/transactions/entitlements/downloads/royalties/disputes.
11. API Tree: asset/search/license/entitlement/download/version/provenance/royalty/status.
12. Monetization Tree: commission/subscriptions/seats/storage/delivery/verification/OEM/API/affiliate.
13. Distribution Tree: creator/developer/design/AI/education ecosystems, integrations, OEM/private exchanges.
14. Automation Tree: metadata/checks/search/entitlement/delivery/reconciliation; publish/pay/disputes protected.
15. Moat Tree: provenance graph, license ontology, creator trust, entitlement history, similarity fingerprints.
16. Platform Tree: marketplace→licensing infrastructure→cross-platform rights/entitlement network.
17. Risk Tree: IP theft, malicious assets, ownership ambiguity, payment/tax, moderation, account takeover.
18. Scale Tree: niche→multi-asset→enterprise/OEM→global ecosystem.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #79/#81/#69/#70 already cover provenance/license compliance/billing/entitlements.
20. Command Center Dependencies: asset registry, provenance, identity, billing/entitlements, policy/security, moderation, company isolation.
21. Design-Now Requirements: immutable asset/version/provenance/rights/entitlement contracts.
22. Build-Now Requirements: generic artifact/provenance and entitlement seams after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: marketplace/customer accounts/payments/CDN/pricing/creator network.
24. Autonomous Mature State: catalog/provenance/search/entitlements/delivery/reconciliation operate automatically; humans handle rights disputes, protected publishing/financial and policy decisions.

# Company 040 — Digital Estate / Account Organizer

**Company ID:** `company:future:040`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:040`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-040-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no account access, password custody, beneficiary designation, legal document execution or emergency disclosure.

## Business identity

Purpose: help individuals/families securely inventory digital accounts, subscriptions, documents, assets, instructions and trusted contacts so important information is organized for emergencies, incapacity and estate/legacy planning.

Problem: digital lives are fragmented; families do not know what exists, where documents are, what should happen to accounts or which instructions are current.

Value: encrypted inventory, expiry/review reminders, instructions, secure sharing and evidence of ownership/status without becoming a password-stealing vault or legal estate substitute.

## Product tree

Digital Account Inventory; Subscription Inventory; Document Vault/Reference Index; Digital Asset Catalog; Domain/Social/Email Inventory; Cloud/Device/Backup Inventory; Financial-Account Reference Index (no credentials); Instructions/Disposition Notes; Trusted Contact/Emergency Access Plan; Beneficiary/Executor Reference Records; Family/Household Plan; Renewal/Expiration Tracker; Secure Document Sharing; Legacy Checklist; Device/Recovery-Key Reference Map; Deceased/Incapacity Workflow Preparation; Data Export/Portability; Audit/Access History; API/OEM for estate/financial-planning platforms; Professional Advisor Workspace.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: account/service type, owner, provider, login identifier reference (not secret), recovery method ref, 2FA/device notes, renewal/expiry, billing ref, asset value classification, document location, instruction version/effective date, trusted contact, access condition, legal-document reference, emergency packet, reminders, proof-of-life/review cadence where appropriate, encryption, access logs, export/delete.

Customers: consumers/families, caregivers, executors/personal representatives, financial/estate planning professionals, digital-savvy seniors, small-business owners organizing business/personal digital estates. Enterprise use is limited; this is privacy-first personal/family infrastructure.
